_comment: Each platform owns its version, source commit, download URL, archive and payload hashes.
Archives are pinned against official GitHub release asset metadata; companion checksums
are additional transfer checks, not an independent trust anchor. Payload hashes inherit
the verified archive provenance and are checked at packaging and before Android launch.
Android v2.1.0 was freshly downloaded and verified on 2026-09-27 for all three ABIs.
Android upgraded to official v2.3.0 on 2026-10-06 (dev.034 mission): archives freshly
downloaded from the official v2.3.0 release and verified against the release SHA256SUMS
9e9c59b188ff235053ae22b9f007f31de3e9bc71c8252ef73b0d626b85b64dae for armv7,
9acd35dc7bafd4bbf0f4bd8337cb26c4efe6ab0d84ec01d1a0a9fa68168b09c1 for x86_64) and the
GitHub asset digests; extracted payloads re-verified against the archive contents and
the embedded 'aether 2.3.0' version string; ELF class/machine/linker and the absence of
libc++_shared.so checked per ABI. The v2.3.0 pt/ helpers are byte-identical to the
previously verified v2.1.0-era helper payloads for every ABI.
Windows upgraded to v2.1.0 on 2026-10-03 (Windows v2.1.2 transformation mission) and to
v2.3.0 on 2026-10-04 (dev.030 mission): archive downloaded from the official release and
verified against the release SHA256SUMS (0cc32dd2...), payload and pt/ helper digests
recorded below. Changing either platform requires updating its complete metadata
together. No fetcher may silently substitute the other platform's version or trust a
server checksum alone. NOTE: upstream never published v2.2.0; v2.3.0 is the direct
successor of v2.1.0 (verified against the official tag list on 2026-10-04).
Built from source rather than downloaded, so there is no upstream archive digest to pin.
The trust anchor is the commit: fetch-android-assets.ps1 clones the tag, then refuses to
continue unless HEAD is exactly this commit, and checks submodule state. The resulting
.so digests are recorded as observed output of that build on the release host - they are
NOT an independent pin, because an ndk-build output depends on the NDK and host, and this
project has not established that the build is bit-reproducible. Treat a mismatch as a
signal to re-derive, not as proof of tampering.
